segments.text: Just when Silicon Valley thought proprietary frontier models like GPT, 5.6 and Fable 5 were
running away with the AI race. China's open weights juggernaut just dropped a nuclear bombshell.
Deepseek V4. And this isn't just another incremental update. With 1.6 trillion parameters,
a radically new architecture, and MIT licensed open weights. Deepseek V4 is delivering
frontier-class reasoning at literally one-tenth the cost of US models. So, how does Deepseek V4
actually work under the hood? And does it finally close the gap with open AI and anthropic?
Let's dive in. To understand why developers on X are flipping out right now,
we have to look at how Deepseek solved the biggest bottleneck in large language models.
Context memory and active compute. First, Deepseek V4 is a mixture of experts model
boasting 1.6 trillion total parameters. But here is the insane part. It only activates 49
billion parameters per token. That means you get trillion parameter intelligence with a computational
footprint of a medium-sized model. Second, they scrap their previous multi-head latent attention
for a brand new hybrid attention system, combining compressed bar's attention and heavily compressed
attention. This innovation allows Deepseek V4 to effortlessly process a massive 1 million token
context window without exploding GPU memory requirements. And if that wasn't enough,
they introduced Ingram Memory, a revolutionary conditional memory structure that's separate
static factual knowledge for dynamic reasoning. Instead of wasting compute trying to recall facts
through complex attention heads, Ingram Memory retrieves data like an ultra-fast lookup table,
slashing latency and reducing hallucinations. So how does this open weights tighten stack up
against American giants like GPT, 5.5, GPT, 5.6, and Fable 5, and dual mode testing. Deepseek

On competitive coding benchmarks like live code bench, complex engineering tasks,
